newsitem.title: GERMANY: New German wheat export deals on hold.
newsitem.headline: New German wheat export deals on hold.

text.p: Export sales of German wheat have failed to materialise this week as old contracts are still being executed, brokers said on Wednesday.
"It's very quiet but prices are holding because of Eastern European export hopes for early 1997...there are already some enquiries," one said.
Domestic markets saw some traders buying from farmers and cooperatives, but many operators started to wind down operations ahead of the Christmas and New Year holidays.
Brokers said prices were virtually unchanged from post-harvest levels.
"Exports to third countries and European millers have not been too successful to date and this means volume pressure, which keeps a lid on prices," another broker said.
But opportunities were seen to compete with U.S. wheat because of the firm dollar, and Spain and Britain were expected to seek German top quality wheat for blending.
Other EU markets were dominated by French sellers, who gained an edge via competitive prices and currency advantages.
The Hamburg grain exchange left its bread wheat price (12.5 percent, 220 hagberg) at 277.50 marks a tonne and maintained its spot feed wheat price free Hamburg at 270.
Export brokers slightly increased the nominal fob wheat price floor, but otherwise kept prices broadly unchanged this week.
Standard spot bread wheat (12 percent protein) was quoted at 284-287.50 marks and higher quality offers moved to 290-305, depending on protein levels.
Barley was sluggish as Danish and northern German feed manufacturers made only sporadic purchases and export markets failed to offer outlets for German supplies.

Brokers said feedgrain markets should be underpinned by additional demand arising from the price stability of competing imported feeds. Feed wheat from other EU origins was likely to compete with German barley and wheat.
Fob rye was steady at 252.50-262.50 marks and fob barley was unchanged at 252.50-262.50 marks, all prices basis December.
